articles.title: Someone built a “mixing board” for controlling your smart lights.
articles.summary:
The F4 is a $1,700 console made of anodized aluminum and solid wood. It has motorized sliders for controlling color and brightness, four buttons for presets, and a knob. (The console can control your music, too.) It works with Home Assistant, Philips Hue, Lutron, and Sonos.
[Media: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yefUGcc3TMI]

articles.title: ‘Nvidia could end world hunger or provide clean water for everyone, now that it’s making over $200 billion in pure profit a year.’
articles.summary:
I can’t stop thinking about that line in my new dataviz story. If the industry wants to show that AI can truly build a better future, why not help fix the world now instead of waiting for “the singularity”? I don’t know about you, but it’d make me feel better about data centers in my backyard.
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/11/in-just-one-second-nvidia-makes-this-much-in-pure-profit-2.png?quality=90&strip=all]
articles.body:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has resigned. What happens next?

articles.title: Samsung’s over-ear Studio headphones leak in One UI beta.
articles.summary:
Samsung’s own software has revealed details of its upcoming Galaxy Studio headphones, according to SammyGuru. The site found files referencing the headphones in the One UI 9.5 beta, seemingly confirming the rough design, 870mAh battery, multipoint connectivity, and wear detection. Head to SammyGuru for more details, including animations of the headphones in action.
[Image: The Galaxy Studio will reportedly have both USB-C and 3.5mm connectivity. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/11/galaxy-studio-controls-featured-cf11cf6f5e.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
